overview.description: The home page keeps only useful runtime summaries and moves shared endpoints and shortcuts away from the main focus area for a denser, cleaner panel.
overview.resource_sampling_detail: Sourced from the shared health snapshot
overview.system_state_detail: UI data has been converted into readable metrics

runtime.description: This page splits runtime details into overview, config, and event sections so the information does not collapse into a single plain-text card.
runtime.last_event_description: The latest event is critical for diagnosing runtime behavior, so it gets its own card.
runtime.panels_description: Switching views reuses the same backend snapshot instead of duplicating state on the frontend.
runtime.entrypoints_description: The shared host lets desktop and browser clients read the same runtime data.

adapters.description: Keep the control-room feeling of the transport page, but drive it from the real shared host, request traffic, and adapter capabilities exposed by Liteyuki.
adapters.shared_entry_description: The shared host serves both the desktop shell and the browser, and future Docker/Web targets will reuse the same path.
adapters.section_description: These panels all come from the same health snapshot instead of inventing a separate frontend transport state.
adapters.listen_address_detail: Desktop and web clients share the same host.
adapters.desktop_entry_detail: Default loopback address for the Tauri shell.
adapters.external_hint_detail: External-facing hint for later Docker/Web expansion.
adapters.request_stats_description: Traffic statistics here come from the same runtime health snapshot.

websocket.title: WebSocket bridge
websocket.detail: Long-lived adapter traffic can stay on the shared runtime host without inventing a second browser-only transport layer.

tcp_http.title: HTTP control plane
tcp_http.detail: Health, logs, and future management actions stay on the same HTTP surface that desktop and browser clients already share.

sse.title: Streaming ready
sse.detail: The runtime already distinguishes transport-facing surfaces, so later SSE or incremental event delivery can extend the same backend path.

commands.description: The commands page follows a panelized console layout and adds local filtering so builtin commands and policy semantics are easier to find quickly.
commands.groups_description: Commands are grouped by real functional boundaries so this layout can later grow into a fuller command-management page.
commands.policy_description: Command policy is still owned by the backend, so this page reads current state without inventing a second frontend editor yet.
commands.policy_line_one: The current command policy already supports enable / disable by scope and remains independent from the /help whitelist.
commands.policy_line_two: Once you decide to move policy editing into Web, this page can expand directly into a richer control panel.
commands.empty_filtered: No commands matched the current filter.

ops.title: Operations
ops.description: Console and reload controls that shape the runtime surface itself.
ops.help: Show commands available in the current scope.
ops.reload: Reload config and adapter state from the backend.
ops.adapters: Inspect adapter connectivity and shared endpoints.
ops.log: Toggle log view behavior in the active runtime.

session.title: Session
session.description: Conversation, LLM, and history-oriented commands tied to the active session.
session.ask: Request an LLM reply through the shared runtime.
session.llm: Manage models, providers, and prompt profiles.
session.resume: Switch into a saved session snapshot.

policy.title: Policy
policy.description: Backend-owned policy commands for command scopes and plugin availability.
policy.commands: Inspect builtin and plugin commands by scope.
policy.plugins_toggle: Toggle plugin availability through backend policy.

diagnostics.description: The diagnostics page keeps an operations-observer feel while reorganizing warnings, notes, event previews, and resource snapshots into a faster-to-scan structure.
diagnostics.section_description: This continues the diagnostics-card feel from the main dashboard while replacing all content with actual Liteyuki runtime data.

llm.description: This page organizes /ask, providers, and prompt profiles as panelized capability blocks instead of leaving them as plain instructions.
llm.capabilities_description: The frontend does not pretend it can already edit providers; it only reorganizes existing capabilities into a console-like view.
llm.panel_entry_detail: Both desktop and web clients rely on the same /ask command path, so the frontend focuses on observability and navigation instead of inventing a second protocol.
llm.panel_provider_detail: Providers are still managed through /llm provider list|add|remove|use, so the frontend currently exposes status and command flow instead of a duplicate editor.
llm.panel_prompt_detail: Prompt profiles already have independent storage; this page keeps the profile perspective and command flow until it grows into a real editor.
llm.workflow_description: The full conversation workflow has not moved into Web yet, so this section locks the real command path and guidance into cards first.

ask_entry.title: /ask entry
ask_entry.detail: The web console stays attached to the same /ask entrypoint instead of shipping a second frontend-only prompt flow.

provider_routing.title: Provider routing
provider_routing.detail: Provider selection still belongs to the backend command path, so the web view focuses on observability first.

prompt_store.title: Prompt profiles
prompt_store.detail: Prompt profile storage is already independent, which makes it safe to expose as backend-backed runtime metadata before editing arrives.

logs.description: The logs page reads recent shared-runtime console output directly, making startup, network, and runtime failures observable remotely without relying on a local window.
logs.section_description: This panel shows the latest 200 log entries by default, prioritizing the unified logger path and critical shared-host / Tauri-shell runtime logs.

plugins.description: The plugins page keeps an admin-console structure while staying strictly tied to directories, disabled lists, and runtime notes that the current runtime actually exposes.
plugins.section_description: All directories come directly from the health snapshot so desktop, web, and later Docker targets read the same result.
plugins.notes_empty: No plugin runtime notes right now.
plugins.disabled_description: Disabled state is still managed by the backend, so this panel remains read-only.
plugins.notes_description: Plugin-related runtime notes surface here first and can later expand into a fuller plugin details page.
